sentences.text: The holotype fossil measures about 11 centimeters in length, with an estimated total lower jaw length of 17 centimeters, though this estimate is uncertain due to damage.
Based on the fossil, Eshanosaurus is estimated to have been a relatively small animal about 3 meters in length.
It is the first known Coelurosauria and an advanced maniraptoran living before Archaeopteryx.
This makes it a coelurosaurian, a maniraptor that lived much earlier than Archaeopteryx, 60 million years before other basal therizinosaurs like Falcarius and Beipiaosaurus.
The type specimen of Eshanosaurus was found in the Lower Lufeng Formation in Yunnan, China, and dates to the Hettangian stage.
Eshanosaurus was described by Xu Xing, Xijin Zhao, and James M. Clark in 2001.
The species Eshanosaurus deguchiianus was described by Xu, Zhao, and Clark in 2001.
The generic name Eshanosaurus is derived from Eshan, and the specific name honors Hikaru Deguchi, who convinced Xu to study dinosaurs.
The type specimen, consisting of three fragments of a lower jaw and fossilized teeth, was discovered in the Dull Purplish bed of the lower portion of the Lufeng Formation in Yunnan.
The specimen is housed in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, cataloged under accession number IVPP V11579.
Eshanosaurus had serrated, leaf-shaped teeth with round roots and interdental plates, indicating it was a herbivore.
The constriction between the tooth crown and root in Eshanosaurus covers part of the root, a feature not found in basal sauropodomorphs.
A wide shelf-like border on the outside of the tooth row indicates the presence of fleshy cheeks in Eshanosaurus.
Eshanosaurus is classified within the infraorder Therizinosauria.
Eshanosaurus belongs to the family Therizinosauridae.
The authors place Eshanosaurus in the family Therizinosauridae based on three distinctive synapomorphies.
The authors who initially described the fossil classified Eshanosaurus as a member of Therizinosauroidea based on six distinctive features of the jaw and teeth.
Eshanosaurus may be a therizinosaurian, and if so, it would be the earliest known coelurosaur.

Barrett concluded, in agreement with the original interpretation, that Eshanosaurus is a therizinosaurid and that its presence in the Early Jurassic has important implications for the evolutionary history of coelurosaurs.
Eshanosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic, approximately 196 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The fossils date to approximately 196 million years ago during the Hettangian stage.
The time range for Eshanosaurus is from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago during the Hettangian.
Some scientists doubt the classification of Eshanosaurus as a therizinosauroid due to the long chronological gap in the fossil record implied by this interpretation.
Sues and Averianov (2016) considered the therizinosaurian affinities of Eshanosaurus to be problematic.
Due to the unusually long chronological gap in the fossil record of therizinosaurs and coelurosaurs, some scientists have expressed doubts about the classification of Eshanosaurus as a therizinosaur.
James Kirkland and D. G. Wolfe reported in personal correspondence that the teeth of Eshanosaurus had a medial crest seen only in prosauropods or basal Sauropodomorpha.
